title: Government bond yield sits at its highest in a year
summary: The average yield on 10 year US Treasury bonds was 4.99% in September, up from 4.06% in October 2025. It has risen from 4.13% in February.
why: A bond yield is the interest the government pays you for lending it money. When that safe interest goes up, investors can ask for more before they buy riskier things like stocks, so high yields can weigh on share prices.
source: Alpha Vantage (10 year Treasury constant maturity, monthly)

title: GE, Meta and Lockheed report results next week
summary: GE Aerospace reports on Oct 20, Meta on Oct 21 and Lockheed Martin on Oct 22. Analysts expect earnings per share of about $2.01, $6.67 and $7.52.
why: An earnings report shows if a company made more or less money than experts guessed. A stock can drop even after good news if people hoped for more, so these days are often bumpy.

title: Big tech reports land the week of Oct 26
summary: Microsoft and Alphabet are scheduled to report on Oct 28, and Amazon on Oct 29. Analysts expect about $4.72, $3.02 and $1.96 in earnings per share.
why: These three run huge cloud and AI businesses, so their numbers show how much companies are really spending on AI. That can move the chip makers that sell to them too.

title: Drug and defense shares rise as chips fall
summary: Eli Lilly closed up 3.5% at $1,251.61, about 3% under its 52 week high of $1,292.65. Lockheed Martin gained 2.0% and Intuitive Surgical 1.8%, while Vertiv and NVIDIA fell.
why: Money moves between industries all the time. When chip stocks fall, some investors shift to steadier areas such as medicine and defense, which shows why holding different kinds of companies can smooth the ride.

title: TSMC beats forecasts and guides higher
summary: The chipmaker said July to September earnings per ADR share were $4.60, above the $4.45 analysts expected, with sales of about $46.5 billion. Its filing also points to October to December sales of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. Even so, its shares and other chip stocks ended the day lower.
why: TSMC makes chips for many AI companies, so strong orders hint that its customers expect to sell a lot. Stocks can still fall on good news when investors hoped for even more.
source: TSMC Form 6-K (SEC) and FMP earnings data
